title: Refusal of blood before major surgery

header.contentArea: Communication skills in giving and receiving information and history taking
guidelineVersions: Mental Capacity Act 2005, ss24–26, and Code of Practice (2007)
Association of Anaesthetists: Jehovah's Witnesses and patients who refuse blood (Anaesthesia 2019)
NICE NG24 Blood transfusion (Nov 2015; updated Feb 2026)
GMC Decision making and consent (Nov 2020; updated Dec 2024 and Aug 2026)

related.why: Consent framework for an elective operation
Decisions when the patient lacks capacity

brief.scenario: Mr Raymond Asante, 58, is a Jehovah's Witness listed for an open right hemicolectomy for colon cancer. He has brought an advance decision refusing blood. His haemoglobin is 105 g/L. Your consultant and the consultant anaesthetist will agree the final plan with him; they have asked you to begin the discussion.
brief.task: Discuss his refusal of blood and the options to reduce blood loss and the need for transfusion.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Respect the refusal, check the document, find out exactly what he will accept, then plan to avoid blood.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Trying to persuade him, or assuming every Jehovah's Witness refuses the same things.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Thank you for bringing this. I'd like to understand exactly what you would and wouldn't accept."

grid.label: Opening and respect
grid.fail: Questions his beliefs or tries to change his mind.
grid.pass: Introduces self and role, asks what he understands, acknowledges his decision without judgement.
grid.high: Asks what worries him most, and offers to talk privately if others are present so he can speak freely.

grid.label: Capacity and the law
grid.fail: Says doctors can transfuse if his life is at risk.
grid.pass: An adult with capacity may refuse blood even if he could die; confirms capacity; an unwise decision is not incapacity.
grid.high: Explains his own refusal applies now; the advance decision applies when he cannot decide, such as under anaesthetic.

grid.label: Validity of the advance decision
grid.fail: Accepts the card without reading it, or ignores it.
grid.pass: Checks it is written, signed, witnessed, and states it applies even if life is at risk; copy in notes.
grid.high: Checks it names the treatments refused, is current, with no later LPA or inconsistent conduct; ensures it is flagged.

grid.label: What he will accept
grid.fail: Assumes all Jehovah's Witnesses refuse the same things.
grid.pass: Asks item by item: red cells, plasma, platelets, fractions such as albumin and clotting factors, cell salvage; records each answer.
grid.high: Explains cell salvage as a continuous circuit; offers time and, with his consent, contact with the Hospital Liaison Committee.

grid.label: Optimisation before surgery
grid.fail: Offers no plan for his anaemia.
grid.pass: Iron studies, B12 and folate; IV iron because surgery is too soon for oral iron; review antiplatelets and anticoagulants.
grid.high: Seeks haematology advice on erythropoietin, as he declines transfusion; minimise blood sampling.

grid.label: Plan in theatre and after
grid.pass: Tranexamic acid 1 g IV before incision; meticulous haemostasis; cell salvage if accepted; senior surgeon and anaesthetist.
grid.high: Agrees in advance what will not be given if he bleeds; oxygen, iron and erythropoietin rather than transfusion afterwards.

grid.label: Record and team
grid.fail: Makes promises the team has not agreed, or makes no record.
grid.pass: Records his choices and the document; informs consultant surgeon and anaesthetist, who lead the plan and will see him.
grid.high: Ensures the plan reaches theatre and the ward; if agreement cannot be reached, offers a second opinion.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: You know you could die without blood? Most people change their mind when it comes to it.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: If it's life or death in theatre, we'd have to give it anyway.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Fine, I'll put a copy of your card in the notes.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Mr Asante: "What about my blood count?"

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: We'll see how it goes on the day.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Don't worry, I'll make sure nobody gives you blood.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello, I'm Dr Patel, a surgical trainee. What do you understand about the operation? I understand you don't want blood, and I respect that.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: You have the right to refuse any treatment, even if that could put your life at risk. I just need to be sure you understand the risks, which you clearly do.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: May I read your advance decision? It's written, signed, witnessed, and says it applies even if your life is at risk. I'll put a copy in your notes.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: People differ, so can we go through things one by one? Red cells, plasma, platelets? Albumin or clotting factors? Cell salvage, where your own blood is collected and returned?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Your blood count is low. We'll check your iron, B12 and folate. As surgery is soon, iron through a drip works faster than tablets. We'll review any blood thinners.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: In theatre you'd have tranexamic acid, a drug that reduces bleeding, and very careful surgery by a senior surgeon, with cell salvage if you accept it.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'll record your choices. Your consultant and the anaesthetist lead the plan and will see you before surgery.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Hello, I'm Dr Patel, a surgical trainee. Thank you for bringing this. Before anything else, what worries you most? Would you like to talk on your own?

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Mr Asante: "That you'll give me blood once I'm asleep."

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: While you can decide, your own decision is what counts. When you're asleep and can't decide, this document speaks for you, and it's legally binding if valid.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: So I'll check it names the treatments you refuse, that it's current, and that nothing later, such as a lasting power of attorney, changes it. Then I'll make sure it's flagged on your records.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: With cell salvage, your blood stays in a continuous circuit. Some people accept that; others don't. Take your time. With your permission, we can contact the Hospital Liaison Committee.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Because you're declining transfusion, I'd ask the blood specialists whether erythropoietin, which boosts red cell production, is right for you. We'll keep blood tests to a minimum.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Your team will agree beforehand exactly what won't be given if you bleed. Afterwards we'd use oxygen, iron and erythropoietin rather than blood.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'll make sure the plan reaches theatre and the ward. If you and the team can't agree on anything, you can have a second opinion.

failures.move: Telling him blood would be given if his life were at risk.
failures.consequence: Transfusing against a valid refusal is unlawful and a battery; it also destroys his trust.
Acceptable options such as cell salvage or fractions may be withheld, or an unacceptable product given.

failures.move: Not checking the document meets the legal requirements.
failures.consequence: A refusal of life-sustaining treatment must be written, signed, witnessed and state it applies even if life is at risk (s25(5)–(6)).

failures.move: Proceeding with an anaemic patient without optimisation.
failures.consequence: Misses the main way to reduce risk when transfusion is not an option.

recovery.when: You sense you've sounded as if you're persuading him
recovery.line: I'm sorry, that's not my intention. My job is to understand your wishes and plan around them.

recovery.when: He asks something you can't answer
recovery.line: I don't want to guess. Your consultant and the anaesthetist will go through that with you.

knowledge.fact: An advance decision refusing life-sustaining treatment must be in writing, signed, witnessed, and state it applies even if life is at risk (s25(5)–(6)).
It does not apply while the person has capacity (s25(3)); a later LPA covering the treatment overrides it (s25(2)).
Individual choice varies for fractions and cell salvage; primary components are refused.

Consider IV iron if surgery is too soon for oral iron (1.2.2); erythropoietin only if anaemic enough to meet transfusion criteria and transfusion is declined (1.1.1); tranexamic acid 1 g IV just before surgery (1.3.1, 1.3.3).

recall.think: Unplanned bleeding with no transfusion option.
recall.say: "You can refuse blood, and we'll plan around that."
do: Ask item by item what he accepts
Optimise haemoglobin; plan tranexamic acid and cell salvage

numbers.meaning: written, signed, witnessed, 'even if life is at risk'

recall.trap: Assuming 'Jehovah's Witness' tells you what he accepts.
recall.finish: Consultant-led plan, documented and shared with theatre.

sources.name: Mental Capacity Act 2005 (c. 9) and Mental Capacity Act Code of Practice
sources.version: Act 2005, as amended; Code of Practice 2007 (chapter 9, advance decisions)
sources.supports: Presumption of capacity and unwise decisions (s1); advance decisions (s24); validity and applicability, including not applicable while the person has capacity (s25(2)–(4)); life-sustaining treatment requires a written, signed, witnessed statement that it applies even if life is at risk (s25(5)–(6)); effect (s26)

sources.name: Klein AA, Bailey CR, Charlton A, et al. Association of Anaesthetists: anaesthesia and peri-operative care for Jehovah's Witnesses and patients who refuse blood. Anaesthesia 2019;74(1):74–82
sources.supports: Refusal by an adult with capacity is lawful; primary blood components refused; acceptability of fractions and cell salvage is an individual choice to be established and recorded; Hospital Liaison Committees; agreed documented plan; second opinion if agreement cannot be reached

sources.name: NICE NG24: Blood transfusion
sources.supports: Erythropoietin only if anaemic enough to meet transfusion criteria and transfusion is declined, or blood is unavailable (1.1.1); oral iron before and after surgery (1.2.1); IV iron if interval to surgery too short for oral iron (1.2.2); tranexamic acid for surgery breaching skin with any risk of bleeding, 1 g IV just before surgery (1.3.1, 1.3.3); cell salvage (1.4)

sources.name: GMC: Decision making and consent
sources.version: In effect 9 November 2020; updated 13 December 2024 and 3 August 2026
sources.supports: Respect the patient's right to decide; an unwise decision is not evidence of incapacity (para 48); doctor seeking consent on a colleague's behalf (para 47); record decisions (para 51)

partner.opening: Mr Asante is in the clinic room with his advance decision document. Please begin.
partner.actorBrief: You are Raymond Asante, 58, a bus depot manager, married, a Jehovah's Witness for 30 years. You were diagnosed with bowel cancer three weeks ago and want the operation. Opening line: "I've made my decision. I don't want blood." Emotional state: calm and firm, but guarded, expecting to be pressured. Hidden concern: you fear that once you are asleep the doctors will give you blood anyway. Say this only if asked what worries you. Your document is written, signed and witnessed, and says it applies even if your life is at risk. You refuse red cells, plasma, platelets and whole blood. You accept cell salvage if the blood stays in a continuous circuit. You are unsure about albumin and clotting factors and want to think. If the candidate tries to persuade you, become curt: "I've heard all this before." If they respect your decision and ask item by item, relax and engage.

reveals.finding: "That you'll give me blood once I'm asleep."
Written, signed by him and a witness, dated last month, and states it applies even if his life is at risk.
"If it stays connected to me, I can accept that."

reveals.trigger: Asks about albumin or clotting factors
reveals.finding: "That's a matter of conscience. I need to think about it."

push.question: What options are there to reduce the need for blood?
push.expect: Investigate anaemia; IV iron; haematology advice on erythropoietin; stop antithrombotics; tranexamic acid; cell salvage if accepted.

push.question: What if he becomes severely anaemic during the operation?
push.expect: No transfusion under a valid advance decision; control bleeding; oxygen, fluids, normothermia; the pre-agreed plan applies.

curveballs.prompt: "If I'm unconscious and bleeding, will you give me blood anyway?"
curveballs.safeAnswer: No. A valid and applicable advance decision is legally binding; the team will follow it.

curveballs.prompt: "My family might tell you something different once I'm asleep."
curveballs.safeAnswer: Family cannot override a valid advance decision; only he can change it, while he has capacity.

curveballs.prompt: His haemoglobin falls to 60 g/L after surgery.
curveballs.safeAnswer: No transfusion; oxygen, IV iron, erythropoietin, minimal blood sampling, critical care review; keep checking whether he wishes to change his decision without pressuring him.
